footer.description: Real-time audio collaboration and secure demo sharing platform for music producers.

problem.title: Sending a demo shouldn't cost you the track.
problem.lead: Two things break every remote review: the file leaves your hands, and everyone ends up in a different part of the song.

leak.label: Problem 01
leak.title: The file walks
leak.body: A WAV in an inbox is a WAV on somebody else's drive. Once it has been downloaded you no longer know who holds which version, and you cannot pull it back.
leak.answer: The track you send already carries your voice, and the link to it expires.

drift.label: Problem 02
drift.title: The room drifts
drift.body: One person pauses, another seeks, a third hears the drop four seconds late. By the end everyone is just asking each other where they are in the track.
drift.answer: One person presses play, and the whole room hears the same spot.

pillars.title: Three modules, one workbench.
pillars.lead: A library that holds the work, a tag that signs it, and a room to play it in.

library.title: Library
library.description: Upload MP3, WAV or FLAC and keep every take in one place.
library.fact2: See exactly how far the upload got

voiceTag.title: Voice Tag
voiceTag.description: Type the line or use your own recording, then drop it into the track as often as you like.
voiceTag.fact2: Or your own recording, up to 10s

liveRoom.title: Live Room
liveRoom.description: Send a six-character code, listen together, and talk it through in the room.
liveRoom.fact1: Play, pause and seek for everyone

voiceTag.title: Your name, every thirty seconds.
voiceTag.lead: The tag is mixed into the track itself, not layered on at playback. Which means the track you send out carries your mark wherever it is opened.
voiceTag.point1Body: Have an AI voice read the line you type — Vietnamese, US English or UK English, male or female. Or upload a take of your own, up to ten seconds.
voiceTag.point2Title: Hear it before you keep it
voiceTag.point2Body: Preview any wording and voice together. Nothing is stored until you decide to save it.
voiceTag.point3Body: The tag repeats on the interval you set, the music dips underneath it as it speaks, and a new MP3 comes out the other side. Your original stays untouched.

liveRoom.title: Everyone on the same bar.
liveRoom.lead: The host holds the controls. Play, pause, seek and track changes apply to everybody, so the room hears one position instead of five.
liveRoom.point1Body: Share a six-character code. Anyone who wants in waits outside, and nobody is in the room until you say so.
liveRoom.point2Body: Comments attach to a moment in the track and surface as playback reaches them. No more “around 1:42, I think”.
liveRoom.point3Body: Turn on your mic or camera and talk it through while it plays, up to seven people in a room.
liveRoom.commentSample: the low end fights the kick here

workflow.title: From uploading a track to listening together: four steps.
workflow.step1Body: Drop the file in and watch the progress bar move, instead of staring at a spinner with no idea how long is left.
workflow.step2Body: Pick a voice tag, then set how often it repeats, how loud it sits and how far into the track it starts. These choices are locked in as you upload.
workflow.step3Body: The tag gets mixed into the track for you. You can follow the status from processing to ready, and retry it if anything fails.
workflow.step4Body: Open a room, send the code, approve who joins and press play. Everyone hears the same second.

trust.title: The things you shouldn't have to think about.
trust.lead: Nobody shows off the privacy and safety work, but it has to be right every time.
trust.item1Body: Every time a file is opened or downloaded, we check it actually belongs to your account first.
trust.item2Body: A listening link only works for a short window. Once it lapses it cannot be opened again, even by someone who copied it.
trust.item3Title: You can see every signed-in device
trust.item3Body: Look through the devices signed in to your account, and sign any of them out with a single click.
trust.item4Body: Delete a track and its files are cleared from storage too. Close your account and your personal details are removed from the system.

hero.title: Three modules, walked through step by step.
hero.lead: Below is a guide to each module, in the order the screens actually appear: where to click, what to fill in, and what you get back. Every image and video is captured from the real app.
hero.techLink: See how it is built underneath

voiceTag.title: Create your own voice tag.
voiceTag.lead: A voice tag is the short audio signature you stamp on your tracks. This guide covers the whole thing: from opening the Voice Tags tab to having a tag ready to attach to a song.

ways.label: How to create
ways.value: An AI voice, or a clip you record

open.title: Open the Voice Tags tab
open.body: Sign in, go to Dashboard, then open the Voice Tags tab. This is where all your voice tags live, and you can play any of them straight from the list. The first time, the list is empty and offers a single Create button.
open.note: Voice Tags is a Pro feature. On a free account you will see an upgrade prompt instead of the list.
open.mediaHint: The Voice Tags tab with no tags yet, and the Create button.

create.title: Press Create and pick a method
create.body: You choose one of two ways: let an AI voice read a line you type, or upload a clip you recorded yourself. Either is fine, and you can always come back and make another tag the other way.
create.mediaHint: The two method cards: Generate with AI and Upload your own audio.

fork.title: Fill in the method you picked
fork.body: The two methods ask for different things. You only need to follow the matching part below.

tts.title: Create with an AI voice
tts.body: Name the tag, type the line you want read out, then pick a language and a voice. When you change the language you will need to pick the voice again, because each language has its own set of voices.
tts.mediaHint: The AI voice form, with the language and voice pickers open.

voice.label: Voice
voice.value: Male, female, or leave the default

upload.title: Upload a clip you recorded
upload.body: Drag a file into the box or click to pick one. The tag name is filled in from the file name and you can edit it. If the clip is longer than 10 seconds, the app tells you right away so you can pick another one.
upload.mediaHint: A file just dropped in: name, size, duration, and a play button.

name.label: Tag name
name.value: Taken from the file name, editable

preview.title: Listen before you save
preview.body: Press Preview to hear exactly what you just filled in. Nothing is saved at this point — if you leave the page, no tag is created. Every time you edit the text, the language or the voice, the old preview is dropped so you never judge the wrong version.
preview.note: Previews are limited. If you press it many times in a row, the app tells you how long to wait.
preview.mediaHint: Short video: press Preview, wait a moment, then the sample plays.

save.title: Save the tag
save.body: Press Create voice tag. The tag is saved, you land back on the list with a confirmation, and the new card shows its name, language and length.
save.mediaHint: The list right after saving, with the new tag card and a confirmation message.

result.label: Result
result.value: A voice tag in your library, ready to use

manage.title: Play, rename or delete a tag
manage.body: Every tag card has a play button, a pencil icon to rename it in place, and a bin icon to delete it. When you upload a song, these tags show up in the picker.
manage.note: Only the name can be changed. The audio of a saved tag is fixed — for a different recording, create a new tag.
manage.mediaHint: One voice tag card: the play button, the inline rename field, and the delete confirmation.

rename.label: Rename
rename.value: On the card — Enter to save, Esc to cancel

remove.label: Delete
remove.value: Asks first, and cannot be undone

next.title: Song — upload a track and attach a tag
next.body: Pick a track, set how often the tag repeats, balance the tag against the music, and get a tagged version alongside the untouched original.

song.title: Upload a track and attach a voice tag.
song.lead: This is where a voice tag stops being a separate clip and becomes part of the track. Seven steps: pick a file, decide whether to attach a tag, set how the tag sits in the music, then listen to the result.

formats.label: Accepts
formats.value: MP3, WAV, FLAC — up to 100 MB

open.title: Open the Songs tab
open.body: Go to Dashboard, then open the Songs tab. The list holds every track you have uploaded, with a search box, a status filter and an Upload button. On a new account the list is still empty.
open.note: While a track is being processed, the list refreshes on its own — you do not need to reload the page to see the status change.
open.mediaHint: The Songs tab: search box, status filter and the Upload button.

file.title: Pick the audio file
file.body: Drag a file into the box or click to pick one. The song title is filled in from the file name and you can edit it. Picked the wrong file? Change file swaps it without making you start the form over.
file.mediaHint: The file just picked: name, size, format and duration.

fork.title: Decide whether to attach a voice tag
fork.body: A single checkbox — Attach Voice Tag during upload — decides the rest of the form. Think it through before uploading, because this choice cannot be changed on a track once it is done.

plain.title: Keep the original as it is
plain.body: Leave the box unticked and the track is stored exactly as you uploaded it. Good for a reference copy, or for a master you tag somewhere else.
plain.mediaHint: The form with the checkbox left unticked.

status.label: Status
status.value: Ready as soon as the upload finishes

later.label: Want a tag later
later.value: Upload the track again with a tag

tagged.title: Pick one of your voice tags
tagged.body: Tick the box and your voice tags appear. Type a name to narrow the list. Each row shows the language and voice, so two tags with the same name are still easy to tell apart.
tagged.mediaHint: The tag picker open, showing language and voice for each tag.

source.label: Tag list
source.value: The tags you made in module 01

missing.label: No tags yet
missing.value: The app points you to the create page

tune.title: Set how the tag sits in the track
tune.body: Four settings, each with a slider and a number box. Above them is a bar standing in for a three-minute track: it marks every spot the tag will land and counts them as you drag, so you can picture the result before uploading.
tune.note: Read Ducking twice: it is how much of the music is kept while the tag speaks, not how much is taken away. At 50% the music sits at half volume underneath the tag.
tune.mediaHint: Short video: drag the repeat slider and the marks on the timeline rearrange.

send.title: Upload, then wait for processing
send.body: Press Upload and the progress bar shows how much has been sent. Once it is sent, a tagged track goes into processing until the tagged version is ready. You can cancel while it is still uploading; after that, let it run.
send.note: Do not want to wait? Run in background takes you to the track's own page so you can get on with something else. The work carries on either way. Only closing the tab mid-upload means starting over, and the browser warns you first.
send.mediaHint: Short video: the stages in turn — preparing, uploading with a percentage, done, processing.

merge.label: Tag merging
merge.value: Only runs if you attached a tag

listen.title: Listen to what came out
listen.body: You land straight on the track's own page. The player draws the waveform of the actual audio: click anywhere on it to jump there, turn on looping, or change the speed between 0.5x and 2x. Below it are the voice tag settings this version was built with.
listen.note: If the track is still processing, the page says so and updates itself when it finishes. If something failed, you get the reason and a Retry processing button.
listen.mediaHint: The song page: waveform player, status, and the voice tag settings table.

config.label: Tag settings
config.value: View only — fixed at upload time

manage.title: Find it again later
manage.body: Back on the Songs list, the pencil icon renames a track in place and the bin icon deletes it. Search ignores accents, and the filter narrows the list to Ready, Processing or Failed when you only care about one of them.
manage.note: Deleting a track removes both the original and the tagged version, and it cannot be undone.
manage.mediaHint: A longer list: inline renaming, the status filter open, and a search result.

rename.label: Rename
rename.value: In place — Enter to save, Esc to cancel

search.label: Search
search.value: Type part of the title, accents optional

remove.label: Delete
remove.value: Removes the original and the tagged version

next.title: Live Room — open it up and listen together
next.body: A six-character code to invite people, everyone hearing the same moment of the track, and the conversation happening right over it.

liveRoom.title: Open a room and listen together, live.
liveRoom.lead: A room is a six-character code, up to seven people, and one track everyone hears at the same position. The guide splits by the role you are in: you open the room, or you are invited into one.

plan.label: Plan
plan.value: Pro to open a room, free to join one

open.title: Open the Live rooms tab
open.body: Go to Dashboard, then open the Live rooms tab. The list splits into Open and Ended rooms and can be searched by name. Two buttons sit above it: Create room and Join with a code.
open.note: Opening a room needs Pro, but joining someone else's does not. Anyone signed in can walk in with the code, which is what makes a room work for a review session with a client.
open.mediaHint: The Live rooms list: the Open and Ended tabs, plus the Create room and Join buttons.

fork.title: Open a room, or join one with a code
fork.body: Two roles, two ways in. Read the part that matches yours.

host.title: Create a room
host.body: Name the room, set how many people it holds, and set how long it waits for you if you step out. You get a six-character code back — that code is the whole invitation, and it stays the same for the life of the room.
host.mediaHint: The create form filled in, and the new room card with its code.

guest.title: Join with a code
guest.body: Type the six characters of the code. Before you go in, you see the room name and how many people are already there; if the room has ended, the app says so. Then comes a camera and mic check, which you can skip.
guest.mediaHint: The code field, the room lookup result, and the device check with a camera preview.

lookup.label: Before you join
lookup.value: Shows the room name and how full it is

devices.label: Camera, mic
devices.value: Optional — join without them and turn them on later

door.title: Wait for the host to let you in
door.body: Once you enter the code, your request shows up for the host, who presses Admit or Decline. Admitted, you are taken in after a short countdown, or you can press to go straight in. If the room fills up while you wait, the request is declined because there is no space.
door.note: Declined three times and you can no longer ask to join that room. Anyone admitted once walks straight back in next time, unless they were removed from the room in between.
door.mediaHint: Both sides: the host's waiting list, and the guest's waiting screen with its countdown.

approve.label: Admit
approve.value: The guest walks in after a short countdown

inside.title: Get your bearings in the room
inside.body: The top bar shows the room name, the code with a copy button, how many people are in, and your connection status. The video area rearranges itself around the number of people. The bottom bar is where you turn the camera and mic on or off, open the participants list or the chat, and leave.
inside.note: A room can only be open in one tab. Open the same room in a second tab and the app asks whether you want to go back to the first one or move over.
inside.mediaHint: A room with four people: top bar, video area, controls, and the chat panel.

header.label: Top bar
header.value: Room name, code, headcount, connection status

grid.label: Video area
grid.value: Rearranges around the number of people

listen.title: Listen to a track together
listen.body: Pick a track from your library and the whole room hears the same moment of it. Play, pause, seeking and volume apply to everyone. Under the waveform, anyone can pin a comment to a specific moment, and it pops up when the music reaches it.
listen.note: You can only pick tracks from your own library, and only ones that have finished processing. While the host is away the music stays paused until they come back.
listen.mediaHint: Short video: pick a track, the music plays, and a comment pops up at its moment.

source.label: Track source
source.value: The library of whoever picks it

moderate.title: Keep order in the room
moderate.body: In the Participants tab the host has two actions: Remove takes someone out of the room and keeps them out for a while, and Mute closes their mic for a set time. Each row shows whether that person's mic and camera are on.
moderate.note: Anyone removed gets a screen explaining what happened, with a countdown to when they can ask to join again — not a confusing error.
moderate.mediaHint: The Participants tab with the Remove and Mute actions, and the confirmation dialog.

remove.label: Remove
remove.value: Confirmed first, then they wait before returning

mute.label: Mute
mute.value: Their mic stays closed for a set time

micStates.label: Mic status
micStates.value: On · muted by them · muted by the host

end.title: Leave the room, or end it
end.body: A guest who leaves frees up their spot and can come back any time with the same code. A host who leaves does not close the room: everyone is told the host stepped out, and the room waits for exactly as long as was set. Only End room closes it for everybody.
end.note: An ended room stays in your list and can be reopened with the same code. Reopening starts a fresh session: the previous participants, chat and playback do not carry over.
end.mediaHint: The host-stepped-out banner with its countdown, and the Reopen button on the Ended tab.

leave.label: A guest leaves
leave.value: Frees the spot, same code lets them back

grace.label: The host leaves
grace.value: The room waits for the time that was set

technical.title: The three hardest problems, and how they were solved.
technical.lead: Not a stack list. Each case below is a real constraint hit while building, the approach taken, and what had to be given up to take it.

library.title: Moving a 200 MB file without choking the API server
library.subtitle: Direct upload with presigned URLs, and search that filters on more than a keyword.
library.problem: Routing the file through the API server means every upload holds a thread and a buffer, and then the same bytes have to travel again to storage. All the user sees is a progress bar that does not move.
library.approach: The backend never touches a byte. It signs a short-lived URL, the browser uploads straight to object storage, and only once that succeeds does the backend write metadata.
library.detail1: Type and size are checked client-side before a URL is requested — a bad file is rejected before any bandwidth is spent.
library.detail2: Progress comes from the XHR progress event, so the percentage is bytes genuinely delivered.
library.detail3: Metadata is written in one transaction after the upload succeeds; a half-finished upload leaves no orphan row.
library.detail4: Search runs directly on PostgreSQL: substring matching on the title, combined with status, format and duration filters in a single query.
library.decision: No resumable uploads. Chunking, per-part state and orphan cleanup are three things to maintain forever, in exchange for very little at the scale of a single demo file.

voiceTag.title: Why a tag at 100% still sounded tiny
voiceTag.subtitle: Measure loudness to EBU R128, match the tag to the song, then mix.
voiceTag.problem: A mastered track sits around -9 to -12 LUFS. A voice tag — synthesized, or recorded on whatever the user had — sits around -20 to -27. That 10 to 15 dB gap meant the volume slider ran out of travel long before the tag was audible: 100% only ever meant "unchanged", never "as loud as the song".
voiceTag.approach: Measure the integrated loudness of both sources, work out the gain that puts the tag a fixed headroom above the song, and only then mix. After that the user's percentage finally does what its label promises.
voiceTag.detail1: FFmpeg pipeline: measure LUFS on both → apply gain to the tag → build the looped tag track → mix down to a new file.
voiceTag.detail2: The gain is clamped between −12 dB and +18 dB. Past that the correction does more harm than good: lifting a very quiet tag only surfaces its noise floor.
voiceTag.detail3: Anything below −60 LUFS is treated as unmeasurable rather than believed — near-silence reports a number that would ask for an absurd boost.
voiceTag.detail4: Synthesized and user-recorded voices share one path once they are WAV files; only the source step differs.
voiceTag.decision: Rendered server-side rather than assembled with the Web Audio API in the browser. The result has to be identical on every machine, and the final mix needs to exist as a file to be shareable.

liveRoom.title: Seven people, one track, the same second
liveRoom.subtitle: The server holds an anchor, not a stream. And nobody can listen in on anyone's signalling.
liveRoom.problem: Everyone is on a different connection with different latency, and anyone can reload mid-track. Pushing the playback position every second would be both expensive and still wrong.
liveRoom.approach: The server neither streams audio nor counts seconds. It holds an anchor: which track, at what position, as of when, playing or paused. Each client derives the live position from that anchor plus elapsed time.
liveRoom.detail1: No process ticks every second to write the position — state changes only when somebody presses a button.
liveRoom.detail2: One event carries the whole state; its type only tells a client whether the audio source needs reloading.
liveRoom.detail3: A sequence number on every event makes a late-arriving frame a harmless no-op instead of a jump backwards.
liveRoom.detail4: WebRTC signalling goes through a per-principal user queue rather than a shared topic — one member's SDP and ICE cannot be subscribed to by another.
liveRoom.decision: Ending a room pauses the music instead of clearing it, against the literal requirement. Undo has to restore the session whole — deleting the row would make music the one thing that did not come back.
